To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
impaired overload‐stimulated muscle growth in aged fast twitch skeletal muscle may partly result, at least in part, from diminished translational signalling.
age‐related decrements in signalling pathways controlling protein translation are associated with impaired overload‐mediated muscle growth in aged fast twitch skeletal muscle.
the impaired growth in overloaded fast‐twich muscle from aged rats is associated with diminished signalling in the mammalian target of Rapamycin pathway controlling protein synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying impaired overload‐inducedskeletal muscle growth in aged animals, with particular emphasis on the role(s) of protein translation signalling pathways.
the mechanisms that regulate muscle growth in response to exercise, and the mechanisms that control protein synthesis in muscle.

the mechanisms that control the adaptive growth of muscle in the context of age‐related muscle loss, a condition that is a hallmark of sarcopenia and a major contributor to the functional decline associated with aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

impaired overload‐stimulated muscle growth in aged fast twitch muscle may result from decrements in translational signalling that lie upstream of the mTOR pathway, and may be at least partly mediated by hyperactivation of AMPK with age.

impaired overload‐stimulated muscle growth in aged fast ‐twitch muscle is associated with diminished responsiveness of signalling pathways controlling translational signalling, including the mTOR‐S6K‐rpS6‐4E‐BP pathway, as well as the eEF2 pathway.
the age‐induced impairment in overload‐induced skeletal muscle growth is associated, at least in part, with diminished translational signaling, which in turn, may be due to AMPK hyperactivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
age‐related decrements in overload‐induced translational signalling are likely to be a major contributor to the impaired growth in aged skeletal muscle.
impaired overload‐mediated growth in aged skeletal muscle is accompanied by diminished translational signalling, which in turn may be partly driven by age‐related hyperactivation of AMPK.
the diminished translational signalling and impaired overload‐inducible growth in aged fast twitch muscle are both associated with hyperactivation of the AMPK signalling pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
impaired overload‐mediated growth in aged muscle is accompanied by diminished phosphorylation of multiple translational intermediates that are known to control protein synthesis and growth.

impaired overload‐stimulated muscle growth in aged fast twitch skeletal muscle is associated with decrements in the phosphorylated contents of mTOR and its downstream signalling targets S6k, rpS6, eEF2 and 4E-BP1, suggesting that the age-related impairment in overload-induced muscle growth in fast twitch skeletal muscles is due, in part, to diminished translational signalling.
the translational signalling pathway is an important potential target for future therapeutic interventions aimed at improving muscle growth and function in older people.
